newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna turns a paler shade of red at polls.
newsitem.headline: Vienna turns a paler shade of red at polls.

text.p: The era of "Red Vienna" came to an abrupt end on Sunday when state elections overturned 50 years of outright Social Democrat rule in the capital and bolstered support for the far-right Freedom Party.

Support for Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's Social Democrats slumped nine percent to a post-World War Two low of 39.1 percent. Joerg Haider's Freedom Party finished a strong second with 28 percent -- a five percent gain on the last Vienna state election in 1991 and its best result in the capital.
"This is a disastrous defeat for the Social Democratic Party," subdued Vienna mayor Michael Haeupl told reporters.
But Haeupl, the second most powerful Social Democrats after the chancellor, withdrew an earlier threat to resign if support for the party dropped below 40 percent.
"I will not run away from this predicament...We will have to undertake a radical reorganisation of the Social Democratic Party in Vienna," Haeupl said.
The result wiped out the Social Democrat's grip on the richest and most powerful region of Vienna and the capital known for decades as "Red Vienna".
Vienna, a showcase for Social Democrat policies with its huge public housing projects and massive health budget, has been a socialist stronghold for most of this century.
Only the fascists succeeded in wresting control from the left after a civil war in 1938. Power returned to the Social Democrats after the defeat of the Nazi Third Reich in 1945.
But on Sunday voters gave vent to frustration at rising joblessness and a perceived increase in crime. Haider also struck a chord with his anti-foreigner invective.
The Social Democrats will occupy 42 seats in the 100 seat state legislature, down from 52 after the 1991 elections. The Freedom Party added another seven seats to its tally, taking 30.
The Vienna result mirrored Social Democrat losses and far right gains in a nationwide poll for the European Parliament.
"The Freedom Party not only won the battle with Chancellor Franz Vranitzky. It also defeated Mayor Hauepl," Haider said.
Vienna's Social Democrats will now have to rely on the support of other parties to carry on governing the capital.

Backing for the conservative People's Party, which rules in coalition with the Social Democrats at national level, slipped to a 15.3 percent low from 18 percent. That translates into 15 seats, down from 18.
The leftist Greens and Liberal Forum party won seven and six seats respectively.
"We will talk (about a coalition) with all sensible people. Unfortunately I can't see any sensible people in the Freedom Party," Hauepl said in the run-up to the poll.
